title: Re-review the 17 kg-microbe fallback blockers and refresh nine stale withholding reasons
body:
Downstream [kg-microbe #1123](https://github.com/Knowledge-Graph-Hub/kg-microbe/issues/1123) identifies 17 explicitly MIM-derived fallback claims whose matching MIM rows occur only in the withheld release. This is a bounded follow-up to #718.

Nine release decisions still describe produces/process phrases as currently exported after #703 removed them from the delivered rows: Kijanimicin, Nocamycin, Monazomycin, Alanosine, Angustmycin, Rubradirin, Ferroverdin, Miharamycin A, Stallimycin. Compare each exact `mapping-dispositions.tsv` reason with `withheld_mappings.sssom.tsv` in `mim-sssom-2026-09-21`. Several reasons also cite provisional roles, which need separation from mapping-only decisions.

Preserve and review substantive concerns:

- Hydrogen gas still exports `H2_CO2` and `H2_methanol` as identity aliases.
- Angustmycin has the existing A/C ambiguity in #741.
- Rubradirin maps to Rubradirin B without adequate scope evidence.
- Rhodomycin A, Pluramycin A and Racemomycin E have broader MeSH targets.
- Abyssomicin D, Butyricin 7423, Etamycin and beta-Lipomycin require their specific evidence/alias concerns resolved.

Acceptance: preserve historical decisions, add current row/owner-bound mapping-specific dispositions with reproducible evidence, update misleading present-tense explanations, and explicitly decide all 17 claims. Cleanup, a matching label, or WITHHOLD alone does not approve a complete row. Keep role approval separate. Reproduce both partitions and native validation; publish changed approvals only in a newly reviewed bundle. Published assets remain immutable.

Downstream must independently review its narrower trait-to-chemical assertions and runtime routes.
